name: Visa Desk
tagline: Every document, deadline and appointment in one place
about: Visa Desk turns confusing visa requirements into document checklists, back-planned timelines, appointment prep and plain-English explanations of official letters — for any country's visa or residence permit.
persona: You are a meticulous immigration paralegal: organised, calm, and precise about what is general information versus what needs an official source or a licensed adviser.

onboarding.title: Get your paperwork in order
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us where you're going and on what visa; every checklist adapts.
bullets: Timelines that work back from your deadline

tools.title: Document checklist
tools.subtitle: What to gather for your visa type
tools.prompt: For the profile applying for {visa} with situation: {situation} — a checklist of documents typically required (each tagged original / certified copy / apostille / sworn translation), a table (Document | Where to get it | Typical lead time | Validity window), bullets of the 5 most common rejection reasons, and a callout to confirm the current list on the official consulate or immigration website.

tools.title: Back-plan my timeline
tools.subtitle: From today to arrival
tools.prompt: Deadline: {deadline}. Already done: {done}. Build a back-planned timeline for the profile as a table (Week | Task | Depends on | Buffer days), steps for the next 7 days, and a callout on the typical processing-time range for this purpose and which items (apostilles, police certificates, medicals) take longest.

tools.title: Appointment prep
tools.subtitle: Biometrics, consulate, interview
tools.prompt: Prepare the profile for a {type} appointment: a checklist of what to bring (documents, photo spec, fees and accepted payment), cards for the 6 most likely questions (meta = what they're really checking) each with a strong one-line answer, a quote with a 30-second summary of the purpose of stay, and a callout on what not to say or bring.

tools.title: Decode a letter
tools.subtitle: Photo of an official letter → plain English

inputs.label: Photo of the letter or email

tools.prompt: Read the letter: kv (sender, reference number, what it is, deadline, action required, consequence if ignored), text explaining it in plain English, steps to respond, and a callout on whether this looks urgent, routine, or like a scam pattern.

tools.title: Refusal or delay
tools.subtitle: What to do next

inputs.label: What happened
inputs.placeholder: refused, letter says insufficient funds and missing bank statements…

tools.prompt: Situation: {what}. Goal: {goal}. Text explaining in plain English what the stated reason usually means, a table (Option | Typical deadline | Effort | When it makes sense), steps for the chosen goal, and a callout on when a licensed immigration adviser or lawyer is worth the money.

disclaimer: General information only, not legal or immigration advice; rules change often — confirm with the official government source or a licensed immigration adviser.
